prerequisites: Good background of Physics and Mathematics, especially on: complex numbers and trigonometry, resolution of systems of linear equations, matrix algebra, limits, derivatives, integrals and solution of differential equations.

learning_outcomes.text: At the end of the course, the student will achieve knowledge and competence on the fundamental theories and numerical applications of quantum mechanics. The student will learn how to derive, interpret, and apply the laws determining the structure and the spectroscopic characteristics and properties of atoms and molecules.

At the end of the course, the student will be able to use the knowledge and interpretation capabilities within a logic and comprehensive framework in order to solve numerical problems and answer scientific questions in the field of quantum mechanics.

The course aims at training the student in problem solving and understanding notions, equations, and results. The final goal is to make the student independent in taking decisions pertaining to the choice of the most appropriate approach for the given problem.
The student will be able to integrate concepts in a coherent framework and to express them appropriately, concisely, and effectively in a talk and using diagrams, graphs and formulas.
The student will acquire the ability to undertake further studies on quantum mechanics and spectroscopic techniques with sufficient autonomy.

syllabus_topics: Techniques and Applications: translational motion of a free particle and of the particle in a box
Translational motion in two or more dimensions
Rotational motion in two dimensions (particle on a ring)
Rotational motion in three dimensions (particle on a sphere)
Atomic Structure and Atomic Spectra: Structure and spectra of hydrogenic atoms
Spectra of complex atoms: singlet and triplet states
assessment_rules: The conclusive mark will be assigned as a fraction of 30 and will be given by the average of the mark gained from the written exam and the colloquium. The mark of the written exam will be the average of the grades obtained in each of the 4 given exercises. The final colloquium mark considers oral and graphical communication, scientific language, content knowledge, and ability to correlate notions. The praise is attributed to candidates clearly above average, whose notional, expressive, conceptual, logical limits, if any, are completely irrelevant.
